summary.intent: Run the plan-phase workflow for phase 41 (package and app versioning and release cycles), which involves research, planning, and verification of PLAN.md files.
summary.outcome: Research was completed manually (inline) after a spawned researcher agent got stuck on Anthropic 529 errors. RESEARCH.md and VALIDATION.md were written and committed; the session ended before reaching the planning stage.

repo: Phase 41 covers package and app versioning and release cycles, with an extensively detailed CONTEXT.md containing ~40 decisions.
The repo uses Release Please for versioning with both a release-please-config.json and .release-please-manifest.json.
The monorepo has both a JS/pnpm workspace (pnpm-workspace.yaml) and a Rust workspace (Cargo.toml), requiring separate dependency graph mapping.
GitHub Actions workflows include release-please.yml, deploy-staging.yml, and release-gate.yml — all relevant to the versioning phase.
The desktop app uses Tauri with config at apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json.
A previous planning prompt artifact existed at temp/plan-packageVersioningStrategy.prompt.md.

code.finding: Written manually by the assistant after the researcher agent was killed; synthesizes release-please config, workflow files, and both dependency graphs.
Generated from the VALIDATION.md template; written and committed at end of session before planning began.

workflow: Spawned background researcher agents are vulnerable to Anthropic 529 rate-limit errors and can hang indefinitely without producing output.
When a background agent hangs, TaskStop can kill it; inline research from canonical reference files is a viable fallback.
The plan-phase workflow has a Nyquist validation ceremony step between research and planning that can be skipped when recovering from failures.
Committing intermediate artifacts (RESEARCH.md, VALIDATION.md) as discrete git commits preserves progress during interrupted sessions.

friction: Anthropic 529 (overloaded) errors caused the spawned researcher agent to hang indefinitely without writing any output.
No automatic timeout or health-check on background agents — the user had to notice and flag it manually.
Recovery required manually reading ~10 canonical files and writing RESEARCH.md inline, duplicating work the agent was supposed to do.
Session was interrupted by the user twice during the recovery phase, adding context-switching overhead.
open_items: The planning stage (spawning gsd-planner to produce PLAN.md files) was never reached — needs to be run in a fresh session.
The verification loop (gsd-plan-checker) and any iteration cycles are still pending.
The Nyquist validation step was skipped during recovery and may need to be revisited before planning is considered complete.
